title: Alsace
description: Between the Vosges and the Rhine: aromatic whites named by grape, from dry to noble rot sweet.
L: In the rain shadow of the Vosges
Explain its French and German history

Alsace lies in north-east France, a narrow strip about 120 km long between the Vosges mountains to the west and the Rhine river to the east, on the border with Germany. Vineyards run along the lower slopes of the Vosges, from 200 to 450 m. Soils are a mosaic: granite, limestone, schist, sandstone, volcanic and marl.

The Vosges block wet westerly winds, so Alsace is one of France's driest regions; Colmar gets only about 500 mm of rain a year. Summers are warm and sunny, autumns long and dry. That lets grapes ripen fully in a northern latitude, around 48 degrees, giving ripe, aromatic wines with good acidity.
Why is Alsace so dry and sunny for its latitude?
The Vosges block rain from the west
The mountains cast a rain shadow.

Alsace changed hands between France and Germany several times: German from 1871 to 1918, and occupied again in 1940 to 1944. Its culture, architecture and grape names show both influences. It uses the tall, slim flûte bottle, required by law, and names grapes on labels, unlike most of France.
Blending 13 grapes is a southern Rhône practice.
Alsace lies between the Vosges and the Rhine
The Vosges rain shadow makes it dry and sunny
Its French and German history shows in labels and bottles

Alsace's four noble grapes are Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat. They're the only ones allowed in most Grand Cru wines. Riesling is the most planted, giving dry, mineral wines. Gewürztraminer gives lychee and rose; Pinot Gris rich, smoky pear; Muscat dry, grapey wines.

Pinot Blanc and Auxerrois make soft, everyday whites and much of Crémant d'Alsace. Sylvaner gives light, fresh wines. Pinot Noir is the only red, increasingly serious. Edelzwicker and Gentil are blends of several grapes. Most Alsace wines are single-variety, unoaked or aged in old, large foudres.
Match each grape to its character.
Alsace names each wine by grape.
Alsace Muscat is usually dry, a surprise for those who know sweet Muscats. It's a classic with asparagus in spring.
Which is Alsace's most planted noble grape?
Riesling covers the most area of the four.
Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat are noble
Pinot Blanc, Sylvaner and Pinot Noir complete the range
Most wines are single-variety and named by grape
Explain the Alsace Grand Cru system

Alsace has 51 Grand Cru vineyards, classified from 1975 to 2007. They cover about 4% of production. Most are limited to the four noble grapes, though some allow Sylvaner or Pinot Noir. Each has its own soil, exposure and rules. Labels show the Grand Cru's name and the grape.

Each Grand Cru has a distinct soil: Rangen, on steep volcanic rock, gives powerful wines; Schlossberg, on granite, gives fine Riesling; Hengst and Zotzenberg on marl and limestone; Brand, granite. Producers argue that site matters more than grape, as in Burgundy, and some top estates don't use the Grand Cru label.
How many Grand Cru vineyards does Alsace have?

In 2021, Alsace began recognising communal and Premier Cru levels, aiming to create a Burgundy-style pyramid. Communal appellations, like Bergheim or Ottrott, sit between regional Alsace and the Grand Crus. The system is still developing.
Most Alsace Grand Crus are limited to the four noble grapes.
Alsace has 51 Grand Crus, about 4% of production
Each Grand Cru has its own soil and character
A communal and Premier Cru level is emerging

Vendanges Tardives, VT, means late harvest. Grapes from the four noble varieties are left on the vine into late autumn, concentrating sugar. Minimum sugar levels are high and set by grape. VT wines can be dry, off-dry or sweet; they're rich, intense and long-lived.

Sélection de Grains Nobles, SGN, is made from berries affected by noble rot, Botrytis cinerea, picked one by one. Minimum sugar is even higher. SGN wines are lusciously sweet, with honey, dried apricot and candied citrus, balanced by acidity. They're made only in good years and can age for decades.
Order these Alsace styles from least to most concentrated.
Later picking and noble rot concentrate sugar.

Even regular Alsace wines can range from dry to off-dry, which confuses buyers. Many producers print a sweetness scale on the back label, and since 2021 rules encourage clearer terms like sec, demi-sec, moelleux and doux. Gewürztraminer and Pinot Gris are more often off-dry than Riesling.
Sélection de Grains Nobles uses botrytised berries.
VT is late harvest, from dry to sweet
SGN uses noble rot berries and is lusciously sweet

Reading Alsace and eating with it

Alsace labels show the grape, the producer, and sometimes a Grand Cru, a commune, VT or SGN. Crémant d'Alsace marks traditional method sparkling wine, France's most produced crémant. The flûte bottle is required for still wines. A sweetness indicator often appears on the back.

Alsace wines suit its rich food: choucroute garnie, sauerkraut with sausages, goes with Riesling or Pinot Gris; Munster cheese with Gewürztraminer; tarte flambée, a thin bacon and onion tart, with Pinot Blanc or Riesling; foie gras with VT. They also suit Asian food, especially Gewürztraminer and off-dry Pinot Gris.
